text:
Alex (support): Heads up — customer AcmePay hit a sudden spike in 429s and latency last night around 02:11 UTC. They say it started after a nightly billing job. Trace sample: trace/01CDEF12345 request_id=rr-9b2c. Can we attribute to route/model/tenant quickly?

Maya (eng-sre): Which tenant_id and route? Is this the hosted API or Dedicated for them? Any client retry pattern visible? :mag:

Alex (support): Tenant: tenant_acmepay. Route: /v1/generate (chat). Hosted API. From their logs it looks like the job retries on 5xx with backoff disabled (so tight loop). I pulled a few request_ids: rr-9b2c, rr-9b3d, rr-9b7f.

Jordan (eng-platform): Start with Prometheus: rate of 429s by tenant+route over 5m. PromQL I usually run: 
```
sum by (tenant, route) (rate(http_responses_total{status="429",job="api-server"}[5m]))
```
Also check per-model token emission: 
```
sum by (model) (rate(tokens_emitted_total{tenant="tenant_acmepay"}[5m]))
```

Vik (eng-ml): The model used for that route is redwood-2.9-large-v1 for them. That model tends to hold larger kv-cache per session and higher tokens/session. If many concurrent short-lived sessions spawn from the job, it can spike capacity quickly.

Zoe (product): For alerting: we should be able to page on tenant-level 429 > 0.5% of requests sustained for 10m, or absolute 429/s > 10 for a single tenant. Those thresholds caught previous incidents. Do we have a dashboard panel that breaks out 429 by tenant -> route -> model?

Jordan (eng-platform): We have a Grafana panel but it was missing tenant label on a few stacks. I'll add a derived panel: "Limits by tenant/route/model" and a heatmap for 429 rate. Quick BigQuery to correlate tokens and 429s (10m window):
```
SELECT tenant, route, model, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(CASE WHEN status=429 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as count_429
FROM `prod_telemetry.requests_*`
WHERE _PARTITIONTIME BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(TIMESTAMP("2026-03-16T02:10:00Z"), INTERVAL 15 MINUTE) AND TIMESTAMP("2026-03-16T02:25:00Z")
AND tenant = 'tenant_acmepay'
GROUP BY tenant, route, model
ORDER BY count_429 DESC
```

Emma (CSM): Customer says their job is a retrying billing reconciliation that spikes every night. They acknowledged it uses a homegrown retry loop. Can we confirm retries caused the burst?

Maya (eng-sre): Check request header for `x-retry-count` or client-side idempotency keys. Also look for repeated client IPs and identical payload hashes in logs: that pattern equals a retry storm. Example quick query in logs: 
```
json_payload.request_hash = "a1b2c3" | count by remote_addr, request_hash | sort -count
```

Alex (support): I pulled logs — many identical payload hashes from same IPs within seconds, and retry_count increments absent (client not sending). So the job retried without jitter.

Vik (eng-ml): Two more angles: 1) Batching/kv-cache: if many fresh sessions hit the same large model, memory pressure can reduce concurrency and surface 429s as token queues fill. 2) Fallback behavior: did scheduler try fallback to cheaper model and get rate-limited too? We should check routing logs for fallback events.

Jordan (eng-platform): I checked routing: there was an automatic fallback to redwood-2.8-medium-v1 for ~7% of requests between 02:12–02:18, but 429s mainly on the primary model. Also saw increased `queue_time_ms` in api_server metrics (peak ~1.2s).

Zoe (product): For attribution we should add a per-request metadata tag that surfaces in telemetry: `x-customer-job-id` and `x-client-retry` so CS can map a single job run to the spikes. Can we make that a recommended best-practice in docs?

Maya (eng-sre): Actionable triage steps I recommend now:
- Create Grafana panel: tenant_acmepay 429 heatmap (route + model) — Jordan
- Add alert: tenant 429 rate > 0.5% for 10m — Jordan/Zoe to approve thresholds
- Ask CSM to ask customer to add jitter/exponential backoff and send idempotency header — Emma
- Create short-term rate-limiting rule to cap nightly job burst for that tenant (soft throttle) — Maya + Jordan

Alex (support): I'll message AcmePay with repro notes and a sample curl they can try with idempotency and jitter: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do
  sleep $(python -c "import random; print(random.random()*0.2)")
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: acct-billing-$i" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2.9-large-v1","input":"..."}'
done
```

DeployBot: Deployment succeeded: add-tenant-labels-v1 deployed to api-server at 2026-03-16T03:05:12Z :white_check_mark:

Jordan (eng-platform): I've created the panel and temporary alerting rule (P1). I also tagged the telemetry pipeline to start storing `client_job_id` if provided. Will follow up with the dashboard link.

Emma (CSM): I'll ask AcmePay to patch the job this morning and report back. Also sharing recommended backoff snippet.

Alex (support): Great — marking this as customer-tentative mitigated. If they still see 429s after patching, we'll consider tenant-specific soft throttles + rate-limited retry guidance. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
